summary: Evaluate privilege-attenuation role behavior across AWS/GCP causing intermittent assume/impersonate failures
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled on-call validation for the new privilege-attenuation role (priv-attenuator) we observed inconsistent behavior between AWS and GCP account flows. Some engineers cannot assume/impersonate the attenuated role and are blocked from running debug jobs against Dedicated pools.

Impact: Intermittent blocking for oncall/SRE when attempting scoped prod debugging. Affects ability to triage Dedicated capacity incidents and perform emergency fixes. No customer-facing outages yet but increases MTTR.

Observed behaviour:
- AWS: sts:AssumeRole returns AccessDenied OR AssumeRoleSessionTag truncated in the resulting session when tag size exceeds ~16KB.
- GCP: iam.serviceAccounts.generateAccessToken returns 403 with message indicating missing iam.serviceAccounts.get permission on the intermediate impersonation service account.

Requested outcome: Determine root cause, provide a short-term workaround to unblock oncall, and propose a durable fix to the attenuation policy and ops-broker role mapping.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From ops-broker in team-ops account, request ephemeral assume of role arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/priv-attenuator with session tags from SRE JIT token
2) Observe AWS CloudTrail event: sts:AssumeRole -> AccessDenied or assume role succeeds but subsequent role session lacks expected tag set

3) From GCP ops proxy, run: gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate --impersonate-service-account=sa-ops@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --scopes=cloud-platform, observe 403 with missing iam.serviceAccounts.get
4) Repeat with reduced session tags (strip long arrays) and observe different behaviour in AWS; no change in GCP until service account binding is updated.
logs: AWS CloudTrail excerpt (2026-03-10T14:12:03Z): {eventName: "AssumeRole", errorCode: "AccessDenied", userIdentity: {type: "AssumedRole", arn: "arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/ops-broker/ebs-jenkins"}}
AWS IAM debug note: SessionTags payload length=17112 bytes; kernel truncation observed in downstream session metadata
GCP Error (2026-03-10T14:18:44Z): "403 Permission denied on iam.serviceAccounts.get for serviceAccount:sa-ops@project"
Ops-broker logs: mapping lookup for principal -> priv-attenuator returned policy with permission_boundary and tag-preservation=false
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 - Aditi: Initial triage - reproduced AWS AccessDenied in prod account. Hypothesis: permission boundary + org-policy tag enforcement causing effective deny when session tags present.

2026-03-11 - Marcus O'Neill (SRE): Captured CloudTrail and STS request IDs. Verified that when session tag payload reduced below ~8KB, AWS assume succeeds; points to size-related enforcement/truncation in our broker.

2026-03-11 - Tanner Lee (IAM): GCP failure unrelated to tag size. Service account binding for sa-ops missing iam.serviceAccounts.get on the intermediate impersonator account due to recent tightening of role grant on project-ops. Proposed temporary grant to sa-ops:roles/impersonate-handler.

2026-03-11 - Hypothesis: Two independent root causes: (1) AWS session tag size + permission boundary interaction causing implicit denies; (2) GCP missing impersonation permission due to change in IAM bindings. Both surfaced together because ops-broker now attaches a verbose set of tags for audit/traceability.
2026-03-12 - Experiment: Deployed ops-broker patch that strips non-critical session tags; AWS assume-rate failure dropped to zero during 2h window. GCP still failing until binding updated.
2026-03-12 - Note: There is an open org-policy in some AWS org units that denies sts:TagSession for roles with permission boundaries; need cross-org policy review.

2026-03-12 - Security/Compliance note: We cannot permanently remove audit tags; solution should preserve required audit information while keeping tag payloads within supported limits or use alternate audit channel.
comments: 2026-03-11 - Tanner Lee: Can we get the exact assume-role API payload and Base64-encoded session tags? Need to correlate with CloudTrail RequestID: 7d2f3b1a-1111-2222-3333-abcdef123456.
2026-03-11 - Aditi Sharma: Uploaded STS request/response and stripped sample tag payload to Confluence (see related_confluence_pages). Also attached ops-broker debug logs to the ticket.

2026-03-12 - Marcus O'Neill: Temporary mitigation applied: created role arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/priv-attenuator-relaxed with identical permissions but no permission boundary and tested assume with full tags; oncall confirmed access restored.

2026-03-12 - Security (Elena Ruiz): Approve emergency role creation for 48h with audit log capture. Follow-up policy change required; file a PR to restrict session tag length via ops-broker prior to role deletion.

2026-03-12 - Tanner Lee: For GCP, applied a scoped binding to grant iam.serviceAccounts.get to the impersonation helper SA. Verified impersonation works; requesting that Cloud IAM owners review project-level role grants to avoid broadening surface area.
resolution: Short-term: Created a temporary relax-role (priv-attenuator-relaxed) in affected AWS accounts and added a scoped iam binding for the GCP impersonation helper to unblock oncall. Mid-term: Patch ops-broker to compress/paginate audit tags and implement a fallback to attach audit metadata to X-Ray/Cloud Logging instead of session tags when payload exceeds threshold. Long-term: Convene cross-org IAM policy review (AWS org-policy + GCP IAM bindings) and update runbook for privilege-attenuation flows.
next_steps: 1) (Owners: ops-broker, IAM) Implement tag-compression patch in ops-broker and land PR #4122; rollout to staging and then prod behind feature flag.
2) (Owners: Security/Compliance) Convene meeting with org-policy owners to review deny rules that interact with sts:TagSession and permission boundaries.
3) (Owners: SRE) Update oncall runbook to include ephemeral relax-role creation pattern and explicit cleanup timeline (48 hours max).
4) (Owners: Platform) Add an automated test to CI that simulates large session tag payloads and verifies assume/impersonate flows across AWS/GCP.
5) Open follow-up ticket to make the relax-role expiration automatic (INT-976544).
